face-wash-for-your-skin-type.before:
A good cleanse is the first step of every skincare routine, and the wrong face wash can undo the rest. Too harsh, and skin feels tight and dry; too rich, and oily skin feels heavy. Here is how to choose a face wash for your skin type, what the different textures and ingredients mean, and how to cleanse.

First, know your skin type

Wash with a mild cleanser, pat dry and wait about an hour without applying anything. Then look and feel:

  • Dry: feels tight, and may look flaky or dull.
  • Oily: looks shiny all over, especially on the forehead, nose and chin.
  • Combination: shiny in the centre, normal or dry on the cheeks.
  • Sensitive: easily stings, turns red or reacts to fragrance.

Face wash for dry skin

Dry skin needs a cleanser that lifts away the day without stripping. Look for creamy or milky textures and soothing, moisture-loving ingredients.

Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash (£12.99, 100ml) combines oat milk with provitamin B5, kaolin and mild cleansers made from coconut and corn. Deyga makes it for dry, sensitive and normal skin. Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99, 100ml) is a soft cream with banana fruit extract, hydrolysed wheat protein and glycerine. Shop every face wash for dry skin.

Face wash for sensitive skin

If your skin reacts easily, keep the ingredient list short and skip added fragrance. The Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash is made without fragrance, and Vilvah describes it as pH-balanced. The Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash is mild too, but it does contain fragrance, so patch test it first. See more for sensitive skin.

Face wash for oily skin

Oily skin likes a foaming or gel wash that leaves skin feeling fresh but not squeaky. Over-washing can make skin feel tighter without making it any less shiny, so twice a day is enough.

  • Vilvah Honey Face Wash (£12.99, 100ml): 10% raw honey with papaya and blackberry extracts, witch hazel and gotu kola, and a citrus-vanilla scent. Vilvah makes it for normal to oily skin, with a medium foam.
  • Vilvah Milk Powder Face Wash (£13.99, 50g): a water-free powder that turns to foam in wet hands, with rice powder, rice milk extract, oat flour, hyaluronic acid and papain, a papaya enzyme. Fragrance-free and made for normal to oily skin.

Shop every face wash for oily skin and more for oily skin.

Tea tree, charcoal and vitamin C face washes

Tea tree and charcoal

Deyga Charcoal Face Wash (from £12.99, 100ml) is a gel built on tea tree hydrosol, with activated charcoal from coconut shell and gentle coconut and corn-based cleansers. It is a popular pick if you are looking for a tea tree face wash: fresh-feeling, and made for all skin types.

Vitamin C

Deyga Vitamin C Foaming Face Wash (£15.99, 100ml) uses ascorbyl glucoside, a stable form of vitamin C, with citron, bitter orange and lemon hydrosols in a light foam. A bright, zesty wash for the morning.

Cream, foam or powder?

  • Cream and milk washes feel the softest: good for dry and sensitive skin.
  • Foams and gels feel fresh and light: good for oily and combination skin. Shiseido Complete Cleansing Microfoam (£29.99, 180ml) is a fine, lightweight foam for everyday use.
  • Powders are mixed with water as you use them, and travel well.
  • A luxury cleanser: Highborn London Crystal Cleanser (£24, 100ml) contains co-enzyme Q10 and is made for morning and night.

How to wash your face

  1. Wet your face with lukewarm water, not hot.
  2. Use a small amount, about the size of a 5p coin, and work it into a lather in your hands.
  3. Massage gently for 30 to 60 seconds, including the hairline and jaw. Keep it away from your eyes.
  4. Rinse well and pat dry with a clean towel.
  5. Follow straight away with toner or moisturiser while skin is still slightly damp.

Most people do best washing twice a day: morning and night. If you wear make-up or sunscreen, cleanse twice at night: once to lift it, once to clean the skin.

After cleansing

A cleanser is only the first step. Add a toner if you like one, then a moisturiser: see our moisturisers for dry skin. Light, soothing layers such as aloe vera gel suit oily skin; read how to use aloe vera gel. Not sure which natural brand suits you? Compare them in Deyga or Vilvah.

Good to know

  • Patch test any new face wash on your jaw or inner arm first.
  • Change one thing at a time, so you know what suits you.
  • Breakouts, redness or itching that last are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

how-to-use-aloe-vera-gel.before:
Aloe vera gel is one of the most searched skincare products in the UK, and it is easy to see why. One jar can work as a light moisturiser, a cooling layer after a day outdoors, a leave-in for hair and an after-shower gel for the body. Here is what to look for when you buy it, and how to use it on your face, hair and body.

What is aloe vera gel?

Aloe vera gel comes from the clear, jelly-like inside of the leaves of the aloe plant (Aloe barbadensis on an ingredient list). It is mostly water, which is why it feels so light: it sinks in quickly and does not leave a greasy film. A good gel is clear or very pale, with a soft, wobbly texture that melts when you spread it.

What to look for in a jar

  • Aloe first on the list. The first ingredient should be aloe vera juice or aloe leaf extract, not water.
  • A short ingredient list. Aloe gels need little else: a thickener to make the gel and a preservative to keep it safe once opened.
  • No added fragrance or colour if your skin is sensitive. A green tint usually means a dye has been added.

Vilvah Aloe Vera Gel (100ml, from £9.99) ticks all three. Its full ingredient list is just four items: aloe vera juice, xanthan gum, guar gum and Geogard ECT, a natural preservative. It is free from harsh alcohols, silicones and synthetic fragrance, and it is made by Vilvah, one of our official partner brands, and dispatched from the UK.

How to use aloe vera gel on your face

  • As a light moisturiser. After cleansing, smooth a pea-sized amount over damp skin. On oily or combination skin this may be all you need; on dry skin, follow with your usual cream.
  • Under your serum or cream. A thin layer first gives your routine extra slip, and serums such as Vilvah Milk Drops (from £21.99) spread easily over it.
  • As a quick mask. Apply a thicker layer for 10 minutes, then rinse or press the rest into the skin.
  • After a day outdoors. A cool layer feels comforting on skin that has had a lot of sun or wind. Keep the jar in the fridge for an extra-cool feel.

In the morning, aloe gel is not a sunscreen, so finish with SPF, such as Vilvah Skin Finish Sunscreen SPF 50 PA+++ (£17.99).

A simple routine with aloe vera gel

  1. Cleanse with a gentle face wash such as Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99) or the Vilvah Honey Face Wash (£12.99). Not sure which? See face wash for your skin type.
  2. Tone with a mist of Deyga Pure Rose Water Toner (£11.99).
  3. Hydrate with aloe vera gel.
  4. Protect with sunscreen in the morning, or a richer cream at night if your skin is dry.

Prefer it ready-made? The Vilvah Sensitive Skin Kit (£29.99) pairs a steam-distilled rose toner with the aloe gel, and the Vilvah Anti-Acne Kit (£25.99) pairs the Honey Face Wash with the aloe gel for oily skin. You will find more routines on our routines page.

How to use aloe vera gel on your hair

  • As a light leave-in. Smooth a small amount through damp lengths and ends to tame flyaways and add shine without weighing hair down.
  • As a soft styling gel. Use it to smooth a ponytail or define curls, without the crunch of a styling gel.
  • With a serum. For very frizzy hair, mix a little gel with a drop of Vilvah Anti-Frizz Hair Serum (£28.99) and comb through with a wide-tooth neem wood comb (£13.99).

For more ideas, see our hair serums for frizzy hair and haircare.

How to use aloe vera gel on your body

  • After a shower, as a light, fast-drying layer on warm days.
  • After shaving or hair removal, for a cool, fresh feel on the skin.
  • Under body lotion on dry skin: let the gel sink in, then lock it in with a cream such as Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99), made with oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane.

Good to know

  • Patch test first. Apply a little to your inner arm and wait 24 hours, especially if your skin is sensitive.
  • Use clean hands or a spatula and close the jar after use, so the gel stays fresh. Check the pack for how long it lasts once opened.
  • Sunburn or a skin condition? Speak to a pharmacist or your GP. Aloe gel is a cosmetic, not a treatment.
